NDT training in Regina, SK: how it works for Regina technicians and employers

Short answer: NDT training for Regina starts with theory that you study online at your own pace, with an ASNT NDT Level III answering your questions, and finishes with a hands-on practical at your employer's own shop or plant. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Regina. The courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A, so they suit employers whose customers name ASNT, and they sit alongside, not in place of, CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification. We reply within one business day.

Regina is a working industrial city on the Saskatchewan prairie. A refinery and upgrader complex, steel pipe and tubular manufacturing, potash operations within driving distance, rail yards, grain-handling and agricultural equipment plants, and a steady flow of pipeline and gas-field maintenance all need people who can examine welds and metal with ultrasonic, radiographic, magnetic particle, penetrant and visual methods. Most of the people doing that work learned the theory somewhere other than a Regina classroom, because there are few full-time NDT schools on the southern prairies. That is the gap an online, self-paced theory course with a practical at the employer is designed to close.

Before you choose any course, settle one question: which certification scheme does the job in front of you actually ask for? Canada's national scheme is CAN/CGSB-48.9712, an identical adoption of ISO 9712. The Canadian General Standards Board stopped operating at the start of April, but the standard stays valid, and certificates are issued by Natural Resources Canada's NDT Certification Body or by CWB Group. Method training for that scheme has to come from a Recognized Training Organization, and Atlantis NDT is not one. Our courses therefore do not count toward CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification. They are built for the other route, ASNT SNT-TC-1A, in which the employer writes a practice, trains and examines its people, and certifies them itself.

If your customer, contract or code names SNT-TC-1A, this page is for you. If it names CAN/CGSB-48.9712, speak to NRCan or CWB Group about an approved course first and come back to us for anything beyond that scope. You can ask about training for Regina with the methods, levels and head-count you have in mind.

How to get NDT certified in Regina: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

  1. Read the work order, not the brochure. Check the purchase order, client specification or code edition to see whether it wants SNT-TC-1A, CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or both. Everything after this depends on the answer.
  2. Get a written practice in place. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer's written practice sets the training, experience, examination and renewal rules. A Regina shop without one can have it drafted; see written practice development.
  3. Finish method theory. Work through the online course for the method and level, using the hours your written practice requires. The training-requirements matrix shows the recommended hours by method.
  4. Log supervised experience. Time spent doing the work under a certified person counts, but only when it is recorded and signed.
  5. Sit the general and specific written examinations. The general paper covers the method itself. The specific paper covers the equipment, procedures and codes your employer uses.
  6. Take the practical examination. This is the part that cannot be done from a laptop alone. It uses real specimens with real discontinuities at your employer's facility, and a Level III grades it.
  7. Pass the vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast are checked and kept on file.
  8. Receive employer certification. The employer issues the certificate, and the technician's file is kept ready for client audits.
  9. Renew on the written-practice interval. Recertification follows the practice, so a technician who also holds a national certificate tracks two renewal dates.

Technicians who would rather hold a certificate that belongs to them than to one employer can prepare for ASNT central certification instead, where ASNT examines and certifies. See SNT-TC-1A eligibility to check where you stand against the hours and vision requirements.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Regina technicians

Every course below is built on the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge for its method. The right-hand column describes where each method turns up in and around Regina so that practical exercises can be chosen to look like the real job.

MethodWhat the course coversWhere it is used around Regina
UT (ultrasonic)Wave physics, calibration, thickness gauging, angle-beam weld work, interpretation against code acceptance limitsWall-loss surveys on refinery piping and vessels, weld checks on pipe and tubular products, storage tank shells
PAUT and TOFDFocal laws, encoded scanning, sizing and data review (Level II, after conventional UT)Girth welds on transmission pipe, heavy-wall vessel welds, corrosion mapping
RT (radiographic)Source behaviour, exposure technique, image quality, film and digital interpretationPipe seam and girth welds, pressure vessel welds, fabricated spools
MT (magnetic particle)Magnetising methods, wet and dry particles, demagnetising, interpretationStructural welds, rail and rolling-stock components, agricultural and mining equipment repairs
PT (liquid penetrant)Penetrant systems, dwell and development, temperature limits, interpretationStainless and alloy piping, non-magnetic components, castings
VT (visual)Acuity, lighting, gauges, weld profile and acceptance criteriaFabrication shops, tank and vessel inspections, structural steel
ET (eddy current)Impedance plane, probe selection, tube and surface inspectionExchanger and cooler tubing at process plants

Level I courses suit people starting out or moving across from another trade. Level II courses suit technicians who already hold Level I hours and documented experience. Senior people who will own procedures and examinations can prepare through the ASNT Level III programme; ASNT itself runs the Level III examinations. Pages for each stage are at NDT Level 1 training and NDT Level 2 training.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Regina

Ultrasonic testing is the method most Regina employers hire for first, because the same instrument measures wall thickness on a corroding vessel and finds flaws inside a weld. A refinery inspector, a pipe-mill quality technician and a fabrication-shop examiner can all be trained on one common core of physics and then diverge by procedure.

The UT course covers sound velocity and attenuation, transducer choice, calibration blocks, distance amplitude correction, and the difference between straight-beam and angle-beam technique. It spends time on the situations that trip up new technicians: rough or painted surfaces, high-temperature piping, couplant behaviour in prairie winter cold, and laminar indications that hide a reflector behind them. Regina's cold season matters in a practical sense. Gel couplants stiffen, batteries fade and instrument displays slow down outdoors, and a technician who has only ever scanned in a warm shop needs to see how calibration drifts when conditions change.

For a deeper look at the method, see ultrasonic testing training. If you are weighing UT against another first method, the usual rule is to follow the work you already have: choose UT if your employer inspects welds and wall loss, MT or PT if the work is surface cracks, and VT if you are in fabrication quality control.

Where NDT technicians work in and around Regina

Refining and upgrading. The refinery and upgrader complex on the north side of the city is the largest single source of in-service inspection work in the area. Vessels, exchangers, heaters and piping are examined at scheduled turnarounds and between them, and the work follows API inspection codes alongside provincial pressure-equipment rules.

Steel pipe and tubular manufacturing. Regina has a long history of steel pipe production for the energy sector. Mills of this kind run ultrasonic and radiographic examination of seams and body, and they depend on technicians certified under the customer's required scheme.

Potash and mining service. The big potash mines sit outside the city, but contractors based in Regina maintain the vessels, conveyors, tanks and structures that support them. Corrosion from brine and fertiliser product makes thickness surveys and visual inspection regular work.

Pipelines and gas gathering. Provincially regulated pipelines in Saskatchewan are overseen by the provincial energy ministry, and interprovincial lines fall under the Canada Energy Regulator. Pipelines are built and maintained to CSA Z662. Radiography and ultrasonic examination of girth welds, and magnetic particle work at integrity digs, all draw on the methods taught here.

Pressure equipment and fabrication. Boilers, pressure vessels and fittings in Saskatchewan are overseen by the Technical Safety Authority of Saskatchewan, and fabrication shops build to CSA and ASME codes. Confirm the current rules with the authority, because requirements for registration and inspection change.

Rail, agriculture and transport. Rail yards, trailer and agricultural equipment manufacturers, and heavy equipment repairers use magnetic particle and penetrant testing for fatigue-prone parts. These employers often have no in-house NDT school, which makes a method course plus employer practical a good fit.

Pay moves with method, level and shift pattern. Our NDT salary guide explains what drives the spread.

NDT schools and classes near Regina: what to compare

People searching for an NDT school near Regina usually find three kinds of option, and they are not interchangeable. A full-time college programme gives a broad grounding over many weeks and suits someone entering the trade from scratch. Short vocational courses run by contractors or inspection companies are quicker but often tuned to that company's own work. An online theory course with a practical at the employer, which is what Atlantis NDT provides, suits people who already have a job offer or an employer willing to certify them.

Whichever you consider, ask the same questions:

  • Which certification scheme does the course feed into, and will my target employer accept it?
  • Who certifies me at the end, the provider, my employer or a national body?
  • Is the practical examination done on real specimens, and where?
  • Are the course hours tied to a written practice or to a published standard?
  • What happens to my records if I change employer?

A course never certifies anyone under SNT-TC-1A. Be wary of any provider that implies it does. If you are unsure which route fits, the NDT training FAQ answers the common questions in one place, and the training overview shows every method and level.

Online NDT training in Saskatchewan

Theory is delivered online on the Atlantis portal, mostly self-paced, with an ASNT NDT Level III available for questions. Access opens the moment you enrol and courses run all year, so a Regina technician on a shift rotation can fit study around work without waiting for anything to start. Reliable connectivity is the main requirement; downloading material before travelling to a remote site is sensible for people who work in rural parts of the province.

Online delivery covers theory only. Practical skill has to be built and examined with real equipment, which is why the course ends at your employer's facility. See online NDT training for the general format, and the Saskatchewan training page for the province overview.

Training a crew at your Regina facility

Employers who want several technicians qualified under one written practice can have the whole programme organised around their own site. Theory runs online for each person. The practical block runs at your plant or shop, using your own instruments, procedures and representative specimens, and a Level III administers the examinations. That keeps training close to the real job and keeps certification records in the form your clients will audit.

Typical starting points are a shop adopting SNT-TC-1A for the first time because a US customer requires it, a contractor widening its method list, or a plant replacing retiring Level IIs. Send the methods, levels, head-count and the specification your customer names through the enquiry form. If a written practice is missing, Level III consulting can supply one, and published US fees are on the US pages; for Canada, contact us for fees in your region.

ASNT SNT-TC-1A suits employers whose customers specify ASNT. Typical examples around Regina are fabricators shipping to US projects, pipeline contractors on cross-border work and suppliers into nuclear and aerospace supply chains. It is not a route into Canadian in-service inspection work that specifies CAN/CGSB-48.9712.

Radiography licensing in Saskatchewan

Radiography is regulated federally in Canada. The Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission licenses organisations that hold exposure devices, and anyone who operates one must hold CNSC exposure device operator certification or be directly supervised by someone who does. Provincial occupational health and safety rules also apply to radiation work, so check them as well.

RT training teaches technique and film or digital interpretation. It does not license anyone to handle a source, and SNT-TC-1A certification does not either. Atlantis NDT does not provide exposure device operator training, so plan that step separately with your employer.

Practise before your practical exam

The Practical NDT simulator runs in a web browser and lets trainees rehearse set-ups and recognise indications in a range of workplaces before they touch real equipment. It is useful for repetition when a specimen is not at hand. It does not replace the hands-on practical on real specimens. For written preparation, use the NDT practice tests, which give method-by-method questions with explained answers.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Regina

How long does NDT training take in Regina?

It depends on method, level and what your employer's written practice demands. Level I and II hours for each method are listed in the training-requirements matrix, and the self-paced format lets you move faster or slower around your shifts.

Is there an NDT school near me in Regina?

Atlantis NDT does not run a school in the city. Theory is online, and the practical is carried out at your employer's facility. If you want a full-time campus programme, look at what the provincial colleges offer and check which certification scheme it leads to.

Can I take NDT classes online in Saskatchewan?

You can complete the theory online. The practical examination cannot be done remotely because it uses physical specimens.

Will this training lead to CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification?

No. That scheme requires training from a Recognized Training Organization, and Atlantis NDT is not one. Our courses prepare you for SNT-TC-1A certification by an employer or ASNT central certification.

Which NDT method should I learn first in Regina?

Follow the jobs you can see. Refinery and pipeline employers lean on UT and RT, fabricators on VT and MT, and process plants on UT and PT.

What NDT jobs are there in Regina?

Refining, pipe manufacturing, pipeline maintenance, mining service, fabrication and rail work all hire technicians. Entry-level roles are usually Level I or trainee positions, with Level II as the target.

Do I need a licence to do radiography in Saskatchewan?

Operating an exposure device requires CNSC exposure device operator certification. NDT course certificates do not replace it.

Does my certificate move with me if I change employer?

Under SNT-TC-1A the certificate belongs to the employer that issued it, and a new employer recertifies you under its own written practice. ASNT central certification is held by the individual.

How much does the course cost?

For Canada, contact us for fees in your region and we reply within one business day. When you are ready, the Register and Buy Now button takes you to the course on the Atlantis portal.

Can you help with Level III?

Yes. We prepare candidates for ASNT Level III examinations and, for employers, provide outsourced Level III support. Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT.
